answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds each identity to a cryptographic anchor via stake burning that scales superlinearly. When minting identities across a clustered trellis graph, each additional agent requires burning tokens proportional to O(N^1.5). Unfolding trust like a blooming lotus, this dynamic proof-of-burn ensures attacking or simulating coordinated swarms incurs polynomial cost explosion, making mass replication economically ruinous.
